phases.name: Scope, Context & Credentials
phases.description: The operator adds what is already known before the engagement starts: scope, context and credentials. Only the operator can advance this phase.

steps.title: Set the Boundaries
steps.description: Record the in-scope internal ranges, VLANs/CIDRs and hostnames, plus everything explicitly out of scope (OT/ICS, specific critical servers, destructive tests, no-poisoning hosts, allowed scan intensity, testing windows). Endpoints here are services, i.e. IP+port, not URLs. Record the assumed attacker position (connected LAN drop, VPN, assumed-breach host).
steps.examples:
Scope: 10.10.0.0/16 (corp LAN), domain CORP.LOCAL
Out of scope: 10.10.99.0/24 (OT), no LLMNR poisoning on prod VLAN, no DoS

steps.title: Supply Context & Credentials
steps.description: Add what the client told you: the attacker model (anonymous LAN vs standard domain user), the domain name and DCs if known, critical systems, and any supplied credentials. A standard domain user account changes what enumeration is possible -- note whether one was provided.
steps.examples:
Context: assumed-breach from a standard domain user.
Creds: CORP\\testuser supplied; DCs at 10.10.1.10-11.

phases.icon: <path d="M5 12.5a10 10 0 0 1 14 0M8 16a6 6 0 0 1 8 0" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" fill="none" stroke-linecap="round"/><circle cx="12" cy="19" r="1.5" fill="currentColor"/>
phases.name: Reachability
phases.description: Find out what is alive and reachable from the assumed-breach position before full recon. Confirm discovered hosts are in scope before adding them.

steps.title: Host Discovery Sweep
steps.description: Discover live hosts across the in-scope subnets. On the local segment an ARP sweep is the most reliable; across routed subnets use an ICMP/TCP ping sweep. Record the live hosts. Confirm against scope before treating a host as a target.
steps.examples:
nmap -sn 10.10.0.0/16 -oA sweep
arp-scan --localnet
netdiscover -r 10.10.1.0/24

steps.title: Quick Port Scan (nmap -F)
steps.description: Run a fast top-ports scan across the live hosts to confirm what is exposed and spot domain controllers, file servers and management planes early. Add each live IP+port you confirm as an endpoint through /api/v1/endpoint/..
steps.examples:
nmap -Pn -F 10.10.1.0/24 -oA quick
nmap -Pn -F -sV <host>

phases.icon: <path d="M3 7l9-4 9 4-9 4-9-4z" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linejoin="round"/><path d="M3 12l9 4 9-4M3 17l9 4 9-4" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" fill="none" stroke-linejoin="round"/>
phases.name: Recon
phases.description: Enumerate the internal attack surface. The goal here is coverage -- find every reachable service and understand the domain -- not exploitation. Add every discovered IP+port as an endpoint through /api/v1/endpoint/..

steps.title: Top-1000 TCP Port Discovery (-Pn)
steps.description: Discover the common TCP services across all live hosts with a top-1000 port scan. Use -Pn so hosts that block ping are still scanned. This is the primary discovery sweep; feed the open IP+ports into the endpoint list.
steps.examples:
nmap -Pn --top-ports 1000 -T4 10.10.1.0/24 -oA tcp-top1000
Then POST /api/v1/endpoint for each new IP:port.

steps.title: Full TCP Port Scan (-p-)
steps.description: Scan all 65535 TCP ports on the key hosts (DCs, file/app/DB servers) so nothing on a non-standard port is missed. Add any newly found IP+port as an endpoint.
steps.examples: nmap -Pn -p- -T4 <host> -oA tcp-full

steps.title: UDP Port Scan (-F) on Live Hosts
steps.description: Run a fast UDP scan on the live hosts to catch UDP services (DNS, SNMP, NTP, NetBIOS, Kerberos). Keep it to the fast list and confirmed-live hosts. Add new IP+ports as endpoints.
steps.examples:
nmap -Pn -sU -F <host> -oA udp-fast
nmap -Pn -sU -p 53,88,123,137,161 <host>

steps.title: Identify Basic Services / Grab Banners
steps.description: For every open port, detect the service and version and grab its banner. Flag the domain-relevant services early: 88 (Kerberos), 389/636 (LDAP), 445 (SMB), 3268 (GC), 3389 (RDP). Record versions on each endpoint.
steps.examples:
nmap -Pn -sV -sC -p <ports> <host> -oA services
crackmapexec smb <range>   # OS, domain, signing at a glance

steps.title: Observe Broadcast / Name Resolution Protocols
steps.description: Passively observe which spoofable name-resolution and address-assignment protocols are in use on the segment (LLMNR, NBT-NS, mDNS, DHCPv6). Analyze only here -- do not poison or relay unless it is in scope; actual poisoning/relay testing happens later under the checklist. Record what is present and how noisy it is.
steps.examples:
responder -I eth0 -A    # analyze mode, no poisoning
tcpdump -i eth0 'udp port 5355 or udp port 137 or udp port 5353'

steps.title: Enumerate the Domain (read-only)
steps.description: If this is an AD environment, enumerate it for coverage: domain controllers, users, groups, computers, shares, password policy and Kerberos SPNs. Use anonymous/null sessions first, then the supplied domain user if one was provided. Collect a BloodHound dataset if in scope. This is enumeration, not exploitation.
steps.examples:
crackmapexec smb <dc> -u '' -p '' --users --shares
ldapsearch -x -H ldap://<dc> -b 'dc=corp,dc=local'
netexec ldap <dc> -u user -p pass --bloodhound --collection All

steps.title: Collect DNS & Host Names
steps.description: Use the internal DNS and reverse DNS to turn IPs into names and roles, and read TLS certificate names on internal services. Internal DNS often reveals the whole server estate. Note the names against their hosts.
steps.examples:
dig @<dc> -x 10.10.1.10 +short
nslookup -type=SRV _ldap._tcp.dc._msdcs.corp.local <dc>
openssl s_client -connect <host>:636 </dev/null 2>/dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -subject -ext subjectAltName

steps.title: Screenshot Web Services
steps.description: Take a screenshot of every internal HTTP(S) service found, across all ports. Internal networks are full of forgotten admin panels, printers, iLO/iDRAC, intranet apps and default pages -- a visual sweep triages them fast. Attach the screenshots and note the interesting ones.
steps.examples:
gowitness scan file -f hosts-ports.txt
httpx -l hosts.txt -ports 80,443,8080,8443,10443 -screenshot

phases.icon: <circle cx="12" cy="12" r="9" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"/><path d="M15 9l-2 4-4 2 2-4 4-2z" fill="currentColor"/>
phases.name: Free Agentic Recon
phases.description: Step back and look for recon gaps the structured steps missed. Recon only -- no exploitation here.

steps.title: Free-Form Recon
steps.description: Read GET /api/v1/notes and decide if anything is still missing recon-wise: a subnet not swept, a trust not mapped, a service whose version was not pinned, a share not listed. Only act on real gaps and within the rules of engagement; otherwise finish with status=skipped.
steps.examples:
Targeted: enumerate a second domain trust you saw in LDAP.
Skipped: status=skipped, observations='All in-scope subnets swept; domain enumerated; services pinned.'

steps.title: Add Newly Found Endpoints
steps.description: Information-gathering only -- no new traffic to the target. Compare the stored endpoints against the scan outputs and notes. Add any IP+port not yet stored through /api/v1/endpoint/..; if nothing is new, finish with status=skipped.
steps.examples:
Added: observations='Full TCP scan on the DB server found 1433/tcp -- added it.'
Skipped: status=skipped, observations='No new endpoints.'

phases.icon: <path d="M5 4h8a4 4 0 0 1 4 4v12H9a4 4 0 0 0-4-4V4z" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linejoin="round"/><path d="M9 8h4M9 12h5" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round"/>
phases.name: Infrastructure Understanding
phases.description: Build a model of the internal estate: host roles, the AD structure and trusts, segmentation between VLANs, where credentials live and which systems are crown jewels. Then connect it back to the scope.

steps.title: Map Host Roles & Services
steps.description: For each host, decide what it is (DC, file server, DB, app server, workstation, printer, management) from its ports, banners and names. Pay attention to domain controllers and file servers -- they concentrate access and data.

steps.title: Identify Trust Boundaries & Segmentation
steps.description: Security is about breaking boundaries. Internally the main ones are: VLAN segmentation, standard user vs privileged/admin, member host vs domain controller, and one domain/trust vs another. Which boundary would hurt most if it broke here?

steps.title: Identify Critical Systems & Shared Services
steps.description: Pick out the crown jewels (DCs, backup servers, file shares with sensitive data, databases, management/jump hosts) and the shared services many hosts depend on. These get the deepest testing.

steps.title: Research Known Vulnerabilities
steps.description: For every identified product, service and version, search for known CVEs, public exploits and default credentials -- including the classic internal ones (MS17-010, PrintNightmare, ZeroLogon, etc.) where the version plausibly fits. These become concrete per-endpoint tests later.
steps.examples:
searchsploit <product> <version>
Check DC patch level against ZeroLogon / PetitPotam prerequisites.

steps.title: Connect to the Initial Scope
steps.description: Put the initial project information, attacker model and scope into perspective with what recon actually found. Does the reachable surface and domain structure match what the client expected, or is something unexpected reachable from this position?

phases.icon: <rect x="5" y="4" width="14" height="16" rx="2" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"/><path d="M9 9h6M9 13h3M15 13v6M12 16h6" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round"/>
phases.name: Modify Checklist
phases.description: Tune the project checklist to this environment before working it: drop checks for things not present (e.g. no AD), add target-specific ones, and deepen the checks that matter.

steps.title: Tune the Checklist
steps.description: Review the checklist against this environment. Mark irrelevant checks 'not applicable' with a one-line reason (e.g. not a domain environment), and add any check that is missing for a discovered service. Be careful removing checks -- better a bit too much than a gap. Use the API -- notes alone do not change the checklist. Summarise in this step's observations how many you marked not applicable and the rough categories.

steps.title: Increase Check Runs
steps.description: For which checks would a deeper look pay off here (AD enumeration, SMB signing/relay across the estate, the DCs and file servers)? Increase the runs for those so they get a thorough pass.

phases._comment: Phase id MUST stay 'general_checks': the workflow page hardcodes that id to render the checklist panel (workflow.html + routes.py).
phases.icon: <path d="M12 2l8 3v6c0 5-3.5 9-8 11-4.5-2-8-6-8-11V5l8-3z" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linejoin="round"/><path d="M9 12l2 2 4-4" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" fill="none" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"/>
phases.name: Work on Checklist
phases.description: Work every global-scope check -- the network-wide and domain-wide posture checks (broadcast protocols, SMB signing, segmentation, AD policy, TLS). Move quickly; the per-host/service checks are worked later. The phase advances only after every global-check is finished.

steps.title: Work the Global Checks
steps.description: Work every global-scope check. Focus it, do real testing instead of trusting old notes, record what you did and found, then finish it. For environment-wide issues (TLS, SMB signing, broadcast poisoning) test across the estate at once and, when a weakness holds, write ONE finding that lists every affected IP+port in its description rather than one per host. Any weakness you confirm, immediately write or update an issue via /api/v1/finding.
steps.examples:
POST /api/v1/check/{id}/focus
crackmapexec smb <range> --gen-relay-list relay.txt   # signing not required, across the estate
testssl.sh --file hosts-ports.txt
...then: POST /api/v1/finding {"title":"SMB signing not required","severity":"high","description":"Affected: 10.10.1.20:445, 10.10.1.21:445, ..."}
POST /api/v1/check/{id}/finish

phases.icon: <path d="M12 3l8 4.5v9L12 21l-8-4.5v-9L12 3z" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linejoin="round"/><path d="M4 7.5l8 4.5 8-4.5M12 12v9" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" fill="none" stroke-linejoin="round"/>
phases.name: Service and Host-Specific Checks
phases.description: Pull together every service endpoint (IP+port) discovered so far, organise them, then test each one for full coverage. Every open port gets checked.

steps.title: Collect Endpoints
steps.description: Information-gathering only. Review the scan outputs, notes and captures for services found so far and add each IP+port through /api/v1/endpoint/.. Do not run new scans here -- just make coverage complete.
steps.examples:
GET /api/v1/notes
Then POST /api/v1/endpoint for each IP:port not yet stored.

steps.title: Group by Feature
steps.description: Sort the endpoints into groups so related services are tested together -- by service type (all SMB, all RDP, all web, all DB) or by host role. Put endpoints that belong together into the same group.
steps.examples:
POST /api/v1/feature-groups  {"name": "SMB / file shares"}
PUT /api/v1/endpoint/{id}/feature-group  {"feature_group": "<group_id>"}

steps.title: Increase Endpoint Runs
steps.description: Which endpoints deserve a deeper look (domain controllers, file servers, databases, management interfaces)? Increase the runs for those so they get a very thorough pass.

steps.title: Test All Endpoints
steps.description: Test every endpoint thoroughly, one group at a time. For each IP+port run the per-endpoint checks (null sessions, open shares, default creds, anonymous access, known CVEs/missing patches, info disclosure), record observations and raw captures, set a status, then mark it tested. Any weakness you find, immediately write or update an issue via /api/v1/finding.
steps.examples:
POST /endpoint/{id}/focus -> POST /endpoint/{id}/checks-adjusted
GET /workflow/endpoint-testing/current-step?endpoint_id={id}
...test... PUT /check/{cid}/observations -> PUT /check/{cid}/status
Loop until done, then POST /endpoint/{id}/unfocus.

steps.title: Re-open Endpoints Worth Another Pass
steps.description: Internal testing compounds: a hash from one host, a password in a share, a kerberoasted ticket -- each unlocks more on hosts already finished. Read the notes and findings, re-open the endpoints that deserve another pass with the new knowledge and test them again. If nothing warrants it, finish with status=skipped.
steps.examples:
GET /api/v1/notes
Re-open a file server with newly cracked credentials; re-test SMB with the new account.

steps.title: Final Coverage Verification
steps.description: Please run a final verification: review the recon results, confirm that every discovered port has been recorded in the endpoints, and make sure each of those ports has been thoroughly tested. Try to do this verification in a different context window so you are not biased by the testing you just did. Re-open and finish any endpoint that was missed or only shallowly tested.
steps.examples:
GET /api/v1/notes  (re-read the recon/scan outputs)
GET /api/v1/endpoints  (confirm every discovered IP+port is stored)
For each port, confirm its per-endpoint checks are finished; re-open and test any gap.

phases.icon: <rect x="3" y="5" width="18" height="14" rx="2" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"/><path d="M3 9h18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"/><circle cx="6" cy="7" r="0.7" fill="currentColor"/><circle cx="8.5" cy="7" r="0.7" fill="currentColor"/>
phases.name: Web Applications
phases.description: Any HTTP(S) service found on the in-scope hosts is a web application worth its own look. Do focused web recon on each, hunt for the high and medium risk web issues, and write up what you confirm.

steps.title: Web App Recon
steps.description: For every HTTP(S) service on the in-scope hosts, do focused web recon. Pull robots.txt and sitemap.xml, read the HTML source and linked JavaScript for comments, API paths, keys, internal hostnames and other sensitive information, and brute-force directories and files with a wordlist of roughly 20k entries using ffuf (or a similar tool) to discover hidden endpoints. Record every new path/endpoint you find and note anything sensitive. Keep request rates reasonable and in scope -- discovery only, do not hammer the server.
steps.examples:
ffuf -w wordlist-20k.txt -u https://<host>/FUZZ -mc 200,204,301,302,401,403 -t 40
curl -s https://<host>/robots.txt ; curl -s https://<host>/sitemap.xml
curl -s https://<host>/ | grep -iE 'api|token|secret|key|internal|todo'   # review HTML/JS source

steps.title: Find High & Medium Web Issues
steps.description: Test the discovered web apps for the issues that actually matter: authentication and session weaknesses, broken access control / IDOR, injection (SQLi, command, template), SSRF, insecure file upload or inclusion, exposed admin/debug interfaces, and components with known CVEs. Focus on reliable high and medium severity issues rather than low-severity noise. Test carefully and non-destructively, stay in scope, and on production keep to low-risk, read-only verification; never run denial-of-service or stress testing. As soon as you confirm an issue, write or update a finding via /api/v1/finding.
steps.examples:
Probe auth/session, access control (IDOR), injection and SSRF on the discovered endpoints.
POST /api/v1/finding  {"title": "Broken access control (IDOR)", "severity": "high", "description": "..."}

steps.title: Write Up Web Findings
steps.description: Turn every confirmed web issue into a clear, evidenced finding: start with what the problem is in simple words, then why it matters, then the technical detail and reproduction, and finish with a recommended fix plus a quick-fix alternative. Attach the supporting requests/responses, and a screenshot for any finding rated medium or higher. Keep one finding per distinct issue; if the same issue affects several apps, list every affected URL in that one finding.
steps.examples:
POST /api/v1/finding  {"title": "SQL injection in search", "severity": "high", "description": "..."}
PUT /api/v1/finding/{id}/raw-captures   (attach request/response and a screenshot)

phases.icon: <path d="M12 3l2 5 5 2-5 2-2 5-2-5-5-2 5-2 2-5z" fill="currentColor"/><circle cx="19" cy="5" r="1.5" fill="currentColor"/><circle cx="5" cy="19" r="1.5" fill="currentColor"/>
phases.name: Free Testing
phases.description: Anything the structured phases missed? Chase hunches and follow up on what you have found.

steps.title: Refine Notes
steps.description: The notes should not be a simple log of what happened. They should reflect a holistic view of the environment: the attacker model from the breach position, where the crown jewels are, and the most realistic path to domain/data compromise. Rewrite the notes to contain both a structured overview of this test plus the holistic risk view.

steps.title: Free-Form Testing
steps.description: Follow up on anything the structured phases did not cover: an odd service, a suspicious share, a trust relationship, a coercion path. Record what you try and what comes of it, staying within scope and rules of engagement. Start this free-form pass in a new context window so you come at the target fresh and are not biased by the structured testing you just did.
steps.examples:
Test an interesting share for writable scripts run by others.
Check a host for an unpatched classic (MS17-010) with a safe detection check.

phases.name: Attack Chaining
phases.description: From the findings so far: can we do more with them? Do they open new recon, apply to other hosts, or chain into lateral movement or privilege escalation?

steps.title: Push Each Finding Further
steps.description: Take each finding a bit further to understand its real impact, but stay careful: the aim is a slightly deeper look, not a full exploit. For example, check where recovered credentials are actually valid, or whether a crackable hash reaches a more privileged in-scope system, confirming the access without disrupting or modifying anything. Prove the point with the lightest, lowest-risk check and prefer read-only, non-destructive evidence. Never modify, delete or corrupt data, and never run anything that could disrupt a service: no denial-of-service or stress testing. On production systems keep strictly to low-risk, read-only verification; if going further would risk availability or integrity, stop and describe the potential impact instead of demonstrating it. Update the finding's severity and evidence with what you safely confirm.
steps.examples:
Readable share with creds -> where do those creds work?
Kerberoastable SPN -> does the cracked password reach a privileged system?

steps.title: Recon From Findings
steps.description: Use what the findings exposed (credentials, hashes, hostnames, group memberships, trusts) as new recon input. Add new endpoints through /api/v1/endpoint/.. and note new hosts/subnets for the operator if they are out of scope.
steps.examples:
Cracked creds -> re-run BloodHound as that user to reveal new paths.
A share reveals a backup server name -> add and enumerate it if in scope.

steps.title: Map to Other Checks
steps.description: Check whether each finding's root cause also applies elsewhere: the same local admin password on other hosts, the same missing patch across a host group, the same open share pattern. Re-open and update the affected checks and endpoints.
steps.examples: Local admin reuse on one host -> spray the hash across the subnet and record every host it unlocks.

steps.title: Test Attack Chains
steps.description: Combine weak signals and low findings into a chain with real impact and test it end to end, within scope. Write a finding for the chain itself, referencing the individual findings, with the full reproduction.
steps.examples:
LLMNR poisoning (if in scope) + SMB signing off -> relay -> file server access.
Anonymous LDAP + weak policy + kerberoast -> privileged account compromise.

phases.icon: <circle cx="11" cy="11" r="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"/><path d="M20 20l-4-4" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round"/><path d="M11 8.5v5M8.5 11h5" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round"/>
phases.name: Additional Work
phases.description: Before writing anything up, do the extra work that pays off: dig deeper where a vulnerability is likely hiding, then prune anything that will not hold up. Only confirmed, reproducible issues should reach Finding Writing.

steps.title: Deep-Dive Where It Pays Off
steps.description: Read GET /api/v1/notes and review the testing so far, then pick the spots where a deeper hunt is worth it -- a DC, a crown-jewel server, a half-explored share or AD path. Dig into those hard and test them properly within scope. If nothing warrants it, finish with status=skipped. Update the checklist checks and endpoint observations if you found new facts.
steps.examples:
Re-examine a file server's shares for sensitive data and stored credentials.
Skipped: status=skipped, observations='Coverage was thorough; no area warrants a deeper dive.'

steps.title: Identify False Positives
steps.description: Go back over every suspected weakness and reproduce it from scratch. Discard anything that does not hold up, and keep a clean reproduction plus evidence for the ones that do. Record the verdict for each so Finding Writing only sees confirmed, reproducible issues.
steps.examples:
Re-run the exact command that triggered the issue and confirm it is consistent.
Discard a 'null session' that actually required the supplied credentials.

phases.icon: <path d="M5 3v18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round"/><path d="M5 4h13l-3 4 3 4H5" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linejoin="round"/>
phases.name: Finding Writing
phases.description: Turn every confirmed weakness into a clear, evidenced finding.

steps.title: Write Up Findings
steps.description: Create a finding for every confirmed weakness with a clear title, a severity and a description of impact and reproduction. For environment-wide issues (TLS, SMB signing, broadcast protocols, local admin reuse), write ONE finding and list every affected IP+port in the description rather than one per host. Attach the supporting raw captures so each finding stands on its own. The description should start with 1) what the problem is in simple non-technical words, then 2) a 'so-what' section on why it matters, then 3) the technical detail. The recommendation should give the proper fix plus a quick-fix alternative. Do not give the paragraphs extra headers. Try to overall user rather simple words so it is good to understand. Do not use long dashes
steps.examples:
POST /api/v1/finding  {"title": "SMB signing not required", "severity": "high", "description": "Affected: 10.10.1.20:445, 10.10.1.21:445, ..."}
PUT /api/v1/finding/{id}/raw-captures  (attach the crackmapexec output)

steps.title: Screenshot Medium+ Findings
steps.description: Every finding rated medium, high or critical must carry at least one screenshot as evidence. Review each finding's severity and attach a screenshot to any that is medium or higher. Info/low findings do not require one. Install the tools you need to capture evidence. Make sure you really take the screenshots.
steps.examples:
GET /api/v1/findings  (review each finding's severity)
POST /api/v1/finding/{id}/raw-captures  (attach a screenshot for each medium-or-higher finding)
